newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ to hear report on alleged Peters assault.
newsitem.headline: NZ to hear report on alleged Peters assault.

text.p: New Zealand will on Wednesday hear a long-awaited parliamentary report into a late-night fracas between controversial Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters and a fellow government MP, officials said.
A spokeswoman for Attorney General Paul East, who chairs parliament's privileges committee, told Reuters that the panel would deliver its report when the daily session starts.
"The report is due to be tabled at the start of proceedings after 2.00 p.m. (0200 GMT)," she said.
The committee, which polices MP's conduct under parliament's internal code known as privilege, started hearings almost two months ago to consider if Peters was in contempt of the rules.
The contempt allegation was made by left-wing Alliance leader Jim Anderton after a fracas between Peters and outspoken National Party backbencher John Banks on March 5.
Banks and Anderton said in evidence that Peters had assaulted and threatened Banks outside the debating chamber after a late-night parliamentary debate on legislation to delay tax cuts.

Peters said he only put a hand on Banks to indicate he wanted to continue talking, but denied it amounted to an assault. He also admitted to having had a "small amount" of alcohol, but said he was not drunk.
Peters leads New Zealand First, a populist, nationalist party that late last year struck a deal with the much-larger National to form the centre-right coalition government.
The committee's report had been expected when Parliament resumed three weeks ago.
Political sources have told Reuters they expect the committee to find Peters in breach of the rules, but it may only require an apology from him.
Banks and Anderton have not indicated how they expect to react to the report's conclusions.
The privileges committee is chaired by East and has four government members, including Prime Minister Jim Bolger, and four opposition members.
East's office said the report was not likely to be debated in full during Wednesday but would probably be scheduled for full discussion by the 120-member house in the coming days.
